content: Bromine monochloride, also known as bromine(I) chloride, bromochloride, or bromine chloride, is an interhalogen compound with the chemical formula BrCl. It exists as an unstable gas with a red-brown coloration. The compound has a boiling point of 5°C and a melting point of -66°C. Its CAS registry number is 13863-41-7, and its EINECS number is 237-601-4. Bromine monochloride is recognized as a potent oxidizing agent. In analytical chemistry, bromine monochloride is employed for the detection and quantification of trace levels of mercury. Additionally, bromine monochloride serves as a biocide, with specific applications as an algaecide, fungicide, and disinfectant. It is particularly utilized in industrial recirculating cooling water systems to control microbial growth. For example, it is the active component in biocidal formulations such as Stabrom 909. Furthermore, bromine monochloride is incorporated into certain lithium-sulfur dioxide (Li-SO2) batteries. Its addition enhances the performance of these batteries by increasing both their voltage and energy density.
